title: Distinguish process-wide access from a container registration lifetime and account for concurrency, disposal, and hidden global dependencies

questions.prompt: Two independent .NET root service providers each register `AddSingleton<ResourceCache>()` and resolve the service. `ResourceCache` implements `IDisposable`, and its disposal releases only that instance's resources. Does disposing the first provider also dispose the cache resolved from the second provider? Explain why.

rubric.point: States that disposing the first provider does not dispose the second provider's cache.
Explains that singleton ownership is bounded by the root provider: each provider creates and manages a separate instance.

questions.model: No. Each root provider owns a separate singleton instance and disposes only the instance it owns.

questions.prompt: A static `Lazy<Counter>` uses its default thread-safe initialization to expose one shared counter. Multiple threads call a method that increments an ordinary integer field using `count++`, without synchronization. Explain how increments can be lost despite thread-safe initialization.

rubric.point: Explains that thread-safe initialization protects creation of the shared instance, not later operations on its mutable fields.
Explains that two threads can read the same count and write the same incremented value, losing an increment.

questions.model: `Lazy<T>` protects initialization, not later field updates. Two threads can read the same count and both write the same incremented value, so one increment is lost.
